passage.title: Playing with my sister
paragraphs: Sometimes I play video games (a)______________, but usually I play with my little sister. She's two years younger than me, but she's better than me. She always chooses a funny (b)______________, like a purple dinosaur or a talking penguin.

When we first started playing, I told her not to worry about the (c)______________. I didn't want to her hurt her feelings when I got the most points. But from the first time she picked up the (d)______________ and started playing, I knew I was in trouble. So now we play games where we don't (e)______________ against each other. We play together and (f)______________ instead. It's the only way I can win anymore!

parts.name: Join with who
parts.instr: Join the two sentences. Use who.
parts.sub: Example: I have a sister. She loves stuffed animals. → I have a sister who loves stuffed animals.

questions.stem: I have a grandmother. She loves to cook.
ans: I have a grandmother who loves to cook.

questions.stem: There is a girl in my class. She loves to dance.
ans: There is a girl in my class who loves to dance.

questions.stem: I have a cousin. He loves to study dinosaurs.

questions.stem: I have an uncle. He likes computers.

parts.name: Rewrite with to or for
parts.instr: Rewrite the sentence. Use to or for.
parts.sub: Example: I gave her a flower. → I gave a flower to her.

parts.name: Unscramble
parts.sub: Put the words in order. Write the whole sentence.

questions.stem: us / grandfather / ice cream / My / for / bought / .
ans: My grandfather bought ice cream for us.

passage.title: Letterboxing
paragraphs: “Letterboxing” is a fun outdoor hobby. Here's how it works: People hide a box with a stamp and a notebook. They post clues on websites to help you find the box. Then you look for the letterbox! You need to have your internet clues, a pen, and paper. When you find the letterbox, you write your name and date in the notebook. Then you stamp your paper. You leave the box where you found it for another person to find.

questions.stem: Letterboxing is a hobby that is done inside.
The letterbox has a notebook and stamp inside.
A person puts clues on the internet to help you find the box.
You put your name and address in the letterbox.

passage.title: Comic Books
paragraphs: Comic books became popular almost a hundred years ago. In 1938, the first Superman comic book was made. Long ago, comic books were cheap, colorful, and easy to carry. The first comic book cost ten cents! After the 1950s, comic books weren't as popular as before, but people still bought them. Today, there are thousands of different kinds of comic books that people can buy. Comic books are still cheap, but they cost a lot more than they did long ago. Today, they cost about four dollars each. How do we know that people still love comic books? In 2014, the most expensive comic book in the world sold for more than three million dollars. That's amazing! Although comic books have changed a lot in one hundred years, some things are still the same. At over 80 years old, Superman is still a popular comic book character!

parts.name: Writing
parts.instr: Write about a hobby you like to do.
parts.sub: 3 to 4 sentences. Dad marks this out of 5.

prompts.t: Write 3 to 4 sentences about a hobby you like to do, such as collecting bugs or fossils, painting, playing a musical instrument, video games, or sports, or taking photos. Explain what you do, where you go, and why you think it is an interesting hobby. Use words and expressions like for example and such as.

rubric.label: Task
rubric.says: You write about one hobby, saying what you do, where you go and why it is interesting.

rubric.label: Theme
rubric.says: The topic is clear and you stay on it.

rubric.label: Vocabulary
rubric.says: You use for example or such as to give an example.
